 5 things to watch in Week 1 of the 2026 WPIAL playoffs: Winless no more, McGuffey ready for return to Class 2A field
 By Josh Rizzo 5 Min Read 
 • Nov. 5, 2026 
 | 1 day ago 
-->
 Go Ad-Free today 
 McGuffey coach Nate Parry (Christopher Horner | TribLive) 
 The McGuffey football program’s return to the WPIAL Class 2A playoffs following two winless seasons in Class 3A wasn’t an accident.
 The eighth-seeded Highlanders will host No. 9 Beaver Falls in the first round Friday and finished in third place in the Century Conference behind the two programs considered the classification’s best teams, Bishop Canevin and Seton LaSalle.
 “The last two seasons, and especially last season, we had to explain to our players to not look at the scoreboard,” McGuffey coach Nate Parry said. “We set small, realistic goals for games. If we had four or five false starts last week, we wanted to not have any the next. If we don’t have a turnover, let’s go and force one next week.”
 The Highlanders only scored in double figures twice last season. This year, McGuffey is scoring 42.3 points per game. The Highlanders have scored 40 or more points in four of their past five games.
 McGuffey also fared well against the Crusaders and Rebels. The Highlanders only lost by seven to Bishop Canevin and moved the ball well on offense in a 56-18 defeat to Seton LaSalle.
 “Even against Seton LaSalle, we had over 400 yards of offense,” Parry said. “We just couldn’t stop them. I’m happy with how things have been going.”
 McGuffey built its attack on a powerful running game. Caleb Simons has rushed for 1,209 yards and scored 19 touchdowns. Denny Furmanek has 853 rushing yards and scored 12 times.
 Parry is excited to see his team’s reaction to being back in the postseason for the first time since 2023.
 “Our kids stuck with it,” Parry said. “They believed in the program, their coaches and themselves. They knew when they were younger and in middle school they were good and were able to get through difficult times because there were brighter roads ahead.”
 Championship coaches in 5A 
 Armstrong coach Frank Fabian would have liked to see the two Hall of Fame coaches who entered the mix in WPIAL Class 5A football take a year to get reacclimated to their surroundings.
 Don’t count Fabian among those who believed there would be any growing pains. When the playoffs start Friday, North Hills and West Allegheny will be in the field, led by state championship-winning coaches in Eric Kasperowicz and Bob Palko.
 Both programs had losing records last season.
 North Hills beat the River Hawks, 14-0, on Oct. 9 at Armstrong. North Hills has a bye to open the playoffs while No. 5 West Allegheny will host Gateway.
 “Neither of those teams are surprises to those inside of coaching circles,” Fabian said. “Those are two Hall of Fame coaches who went to programs who have been historically good and had a few down years. They woke up sleeping giants. Trust me, I wish Kasperowicz would have taken a year to get things going.”
 The River Hawks weathered a difficult final month and grabbed a wild-card berth in large part due to a wild Oct. 2 road win over Plum. Armstrong beat the Mustangs, 38-35, but only after Kayden Lewis returned a kickoff 90 yards for a touchdown in the final minute.
 “That was one of the craziest games I’ve ever coached,” Fabian said. “It spoke to the kids’ resilience. Any time they get knocked down, they get back up. Everyone knows 5A is a meat grinder.”
 The River Hawks lost three of their final four games. Armstrong had quarterback Jaydon Oliver, who has thrown for 1,557 yards and 11 touchdowns, miss some time due to an injury. He will be back for the postseason.
 When Armstrong lost to Moon two weeks ago, Fabian said he was nervous about having to go to the committee.
 Armstrong, which is seeded 11th, will take on No. 6 Woodland Hills on Friday at the Wolvarena.
 “When you get put into the tournament, there’s a little bit of juice that comes with that,” Fabian said. “We have another shot. Woodland Hills is a good program and we were in a conference with them for the last two years. We were in close games with them the past two years, even though the scoreboard didn’t say it. Scoop (Smith) took over those games.”
 While defending WPIAL runner-up and top seed Pine-Richland casts a large shadow over the field, there will be plenty of room for intriguing coaching matchups. In addition to Palko and Kasperowicz, Penn-Trafford’s John Ruane, Thomas Jefferson’s Bill Cherpak and the Rams’ Jon LeDonne have all led programs to state championships. LeDonne won at Penn Hills and Pine-Richland. Gateway’s Don Holl won a WPIAL championship and was a state runner-up.
 Which round is it? 
 Since the PIAA expanded to six classes in football, it has forced the WPIAL to adjust how many teams make the playoffs in each classification to help coordinate the champions eventually entering the state tournament.
 Class 4A will start off in the quarterfinals, with all eight teams in action. In Class 6A, the teams will all have a week off before the start of the playoffs. Only in Class 3A and Class A, which each has 16 entrants, will every team be in action Friday.
 In Class 5A and 2A, some teams will have byes to open up the postseason.
 Bounce-back time 
 Elizabeth Forward and Highlands both had opportunities to claim their respective conference titles with a win in Week 10. The Warriors (8-2) lost a 29-28 heartbreaker to Belle Vernon, while the Golden Rams (7-3, 4-2) were tripped up 38-17 by North Catholic.
 Highlands has a dangerous offense, led by the WPIAL rusher champion Tevin Owen-Cratsenberg, who finished the season with 2,586 rushing yards.
 The Warriors have dual-threat quarterback Kaden Allen, who has passed for 977 yards and added 1,220 on the ground. Elizabeth Forward’s Rocco Thompson has rushed for 1,220 yards.
 No Peel 
 Beaver quarterback Jaivin Peel was declared ineligible for the WPIAL playoffs due to the PIAA’s transfer rules. Peel threw for 1,919 yards as a senior with 19 touchdown passses. Solomon Kail had the second-most passing attempts for Beaver this season with four.
 The Bobcats (4-6) will open the Class 3A playoffs against Allegheny Seven champion North Catholic (7-3).
